summary: Lists the libraries the frontend uses and the commands to run, build, check, lint, and preview it.
purpose: The recipe for the frontend: what it needs and how to run it.
why: Standard for JavaScript projects. The scripts provide shortcuts for common tasks.
how: It marks the app as private and a module. It lists the runtime libraries for screens, styling, state, animation, charts, forms, diagrams, icons, and notifications. It lists the build, type, and lint tools. Then it lists the scripts: dev, build, build check, preview, and lint.
inputs: The package manager installs the listed libraries during setup.
outputs: Commands that run the dev server, create the production build, check types, lint, and preview the build.
risks: Two diagram libraries are listed: the older react-flow-renderer and the newer @reactflow packages. Some listed libraries, such as charts, forms, and notifications, may not be used by the code shown here; this was not verified. The build command does not type-check; only the build check command does.
debug: If a command fails after install, check the version numbers and whether install finished. Run the build check to see type errors. A lock file was not shown, so the exact installed versions could differ.
